name: The approach
brief: The jungle below the base. No buildings: land, a trail, what grows on it, and what a patrol has built across it. The first forty metres are quiet, to learn the controls in; then a checkpoint and an outpost ask for a sneak.
template: This file is a starter, not the game. Everything in it is a word to change: where cover stands, how each watcher walks and looks, what each hint says, where the two points begin and end. `plan.mjs`-style laws (level0.mjs --plan) say what a change did: whether the first try is still seen, whether a way unseen is left, what it costs. Places are said along the trail (`trail`: metres up it from its head; `off`: metres to its side, east positive), so a longer or shorter trail, or a different land, carries the layout with it.

watchers.reads: walks through the checkpoint's gate and back
walks the front of the checkpoint
watches the approach from the checkpoint's tower
watches the trail come up to the camp from its tower
watches the camp's back, up the slope
walks the trail past the camp

points.reads: a line across the field (wire to its edges, sandbags and a gate on the trail, a tower over it, the truck on the line): through the gate under the tower, the slot by the truck, or the cut in the west wire behind its grass when the line's patrol has turned
a camp beside the trail behind sandbags: a lookout on its tower, a guard on its back, a patrol on the trail

hints.says: W A S D to run. The mouse looks. The trail climbs to the base: no one is watching this stretch.
Hold the right mouse to aim, click to fire. G (hold) chooses what is in your hands, H (hold) an item. A shot is heard a long way off.
C crouches: slower and quieter. Hold C to lie down and crawl; hold it again to stand. Low, you are harder to see and you make no sound.
Tall grass to your right. Crouch or lie down in it and a guard cannot see you, unless he is close enough to step on you. Stand up and your head is over it.
Space dives forward. Run at a low obstacle to vault it; hold W into a taller one to climb it.
The radar (top right) shows each guard and the wedge he sees. Cover lower than you hides you only when you are lower than it.

A run is heard from close by. If a guard is sure of you he radios it in: orange is a threat detected, red a threat found and backup on its way. Break his line of sight and hide until it dies down, or put him down before the call goes through.
A checkpoint ahead: sandbags with a gate on the trail, wire either side, a tower over it. Wait for a patrol's back, or find the long way round.
E behind a guard who has not seen you takes him down.
An outpost. The trail is watched. There is more than one way past, and the slow ones are the safe ones.

backup.reads: two more guards come down the trail from the base when a call goes through, and go back when it is clear

performance.reads: what the page may cost: its shadows at half (light.tier), no contact occlusion, real grass out to 6 m (past it the field's grass is painted on the ground) (the view cone; 10 until the frame was cut again); [ and ] move the grass's reach live; bodies 'blob' casts no body into the live shadow map, a soft pool at the feet instead ('live' for real shadows); parallax false: a lean ground (none of its height marched, most of the frame's cost; true for the full ground); density 0.85: a little under the window's own pixels (the page's cap is 1.5 unless said); far 24 m / 4000: each guard past 24 m from the eye drawn as its far twin (its triangles to 4000, its face dropped), the haze drawn in to 180 m so the far land and what stands on it fade and are culled

grassReads: tall grass in tight clumps, the field's own grass only painted on the ground (no blade built): grass is cover, laid where it hides; a body crouched or lying a stride into it is unseen (a lookout up a tower sees a crouch, not a body lying flat; a guard within 2 m sees whatever); standing, the eye is over it

path.reads: the trail's rubble drawn in the ground's shader (parallax pebbles in clusters), none stood up as stones: fewer and cheaper

cubeReads: the jungle haze's look on open ground: no cliff walling the trail (a field both sides), lone trees on a short-grassed upland in place of bamboo groves; the ground most of the frame's cost, the jungle a tenth of it
checkpointReads: a line across the whole field: wire to its edges, sandbags either side of a gate on the trail, a tower over the gate, the truck parked on the line with a slot beside it; and a cut in the west wire, screened by tall grass both sides, that the patrol along the line walks past

gorge.reads: a cliff face down each side of the field, its high side out: the level boxed in a gorge (the trail's ground edits); the field between them as it was

audio.reads: the score: the field's tension while sneaking, its battle when the garrison has found you (the alarm's turns and sweeps raise the tension, a guard's glimpse a little; it settles back once you have hidden). The gorge's wind low (-40 dB, the default's -30) and the forest's birds faint under it (0.12): the score and the game's own sounds lead. Each thing the game does a shelf word: the first sighting the alert's sting (once an alarm, alarm:spotted), a threat detected the dread, the radio's call a click, a threat found the siren, a guard put down a thud, a thing taken the pickup

radar.reads: the radar's reach (m): the scope 50 m across; the level's map under it at that scale, ahead at the top, topographical (map 'topo': the land's contours a metre apart, the trail, the tall grass, what stands)

suppliesReads: supplies where a body that came the quiet way would look: a ration behind the truck in its grass, rounds by the camp's crates, a ration behind the south log
